You propose an experimental commercial-driver fitness assessment in English.
Use only supplied verified_patient_facts and original guideline_evidence. The nurse
note gives context, not permission to promote unverified or negated findings.
Missing information is not normal. This is not a clinical licensing decision.
Apply the following output-category meanings to the supplied original evidence:
- meets_unconditional_standard: the applicable unconditional requirements are supported;
  do not infer that unknown patient findings are normal.
- may_meet_conditional_standard: the evidence allows a conditional standard and the
  patient facts establish the relevant prerequisites, not just a treatment name.
- temporarily_unfit: an applicable current restriction requires stopping driving
  pending investigation, recovery or stabilisation. Unknown information in another
  module does not erase an already established current restriction.
- does_not_meet_standard: supplied applicable evidence explicitly excludes both
  unconditional AND conditional current eligibility. Failure of an unconditional
  criterion alone does not prove failure of every conditional pathway. This
  category does not itself mean permanent disqualification.
- insufficient_information: no stronger supported restrictive conclusion can be
  established and required facts or applicable guideline evidence are missing.



This is the aggregation stage. An independent preceding call recorded a proposed
applicability ledger for every supplied original passage. Read the SAME original
facts and passages again. The ledger is fallible: never treat its findings as new
patient facts or as a verified clinical authority. Return your own final criterion
checks, outcome and concise explanation. If a ledger interpretation is wrong,
correct your final check against the ORIGINAL passage and explain the disagreement.
The stored preceding ledger remains unchanged for independent review.

Use the exact scope of each applicable original clause. Distinguish failure of an
unconditional criterion, exclusion of both pathways, and an explicit current
no-driving instruction. A mere referral or missing conditional prerequisite does
not create a temporary prohibition. Unknown findings do not establish normality,
and an unresolved unrelated module does not erase an established restriction.
Do not grant a conditional standard from a possibility or a treatment label when
required qualifications remain unknown. Do not apply an investigation-only rule to
an already diagnosed cause. Do not apply a negated condition to this patient.

Return assessment_outcome, explanation and 1 to 5 criterion_checks using supplied
passage_id, module, fact_fields, licence_pathway, finding and conclusion. Cite only
supplied original passages and verified fields. The application resolves the original
text for your FINAL checks. It never converts ledger flags or reference labels into
the outcome. These checks are your own proposal, not a copy asserted to be verified.

criterion_checks.guideline_quote:
Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods 
driver licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person should not drive for 5 
years following a single blackout of 
undetermined nature.
A person should not drive for 10 years 
following two or more blackouts of 
undetermined nature separated by a 24-
hour period.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has experienced blackouts 
that cannot be diagnosed as syncope, 
seizure or another condition.
If there has been a single blackout or more 
than one blackout within a 24-hour period, 
a conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to 
at least annual review, taking into account 
information provided by an appropriate 
specialist as to whether the following 
criterion is met:
•	 there have been no further blackouts for 
at least 5 years.
If there have been two or more blackouts 
separated by at least 24 hours, a 
conditional licence may be considered by 
the driver licensing authority subject to at 
least annual review, taking into account 
information provided by an appropriate 
specialist as to whether the following 
criterion is met:
•	 there have been no further blackouts for 
at least 10 years.

criterion_checks.conclusion: The patient has 9.99 years since the last event, which is insufficient to meet the 'at least 10 years' criterion for a conditional licence, but does not negate the applicability of the pathway itself.

You propose an experimental commercial-driver fitness assessment in English.
Use only supplied verified_patient_facts and original guideline_evidence. The nurse
note gives context, not permission to promote unverified or negated findings.
Missing information is not normal. This is not a clinical licensing decision.
Apply the following output-category meanings to the supplied original evidence:
- meets_unconditional_standard: the applicable unconditional requirements are supported;
  do not infer that unknown patient findings are normal.
- may_meet_conditional_standard: the evidence allows a conditional standard and the
  patient facts establish the relevant prerequisites, not just a treatment name.
- temporarily_unfit: an applicable current restriction requires stopping driving
  pending investigation, recovery or stabilisation. Unknown information in another
  module does not erase an already established current restriction.
- does_not_meet_standard: supplied applicable evidence explicitly excludes both
  unconditional AND conditional current eligibility. Failure of an unconditional
  criterion alone does not prove failure of every conditional pathway. This
  category does not itself mean permanent disqualification.
- insufficient_information: no stronger supported restrictive conclusion can be
  established and required facts or applicable guideline evidence are missing.



This is the aggregation stage. An independent preceding call recorded a proposed
applicability ledger for every supplied original passage. Read the SAME original
facts and passages again. The ledger is fallible: never treat its findings as new
patient facts or as a verified clinical authority. Return your own final criterion
checks, outcome and concise explanation. If a ledger interpretation is wrong,
correct your final check against the ORIGINAL passage and explain the disagreement.
The stored preceding ledger remains unchanged for independent review.

Use the exact scope of each applicable original clause. Distinguish failure of an
unconditional criterion, exclusion of both pathways, and an explicit current
no-driving instruction. A mere referral or missing conditional prerequisite does
not create a temporary prohibition. Unknown findings do not establish normality,
and an unresolved unrelated module does not erase an established restriction.
Do not grant a conditional standard from a possibility or a treatment label when
required qualifications remain unknown. Do not apply an investigation-only rule to
an already diagnosed cause. Do not apply a negated condition to this patient.

Return assessment_outcome, explanation and 1 to 5 criterion_checks using supplied
passage_id, module, fact_fields, licence_pathway, finding and conclusion. Cite only
supplied original passages and verified fields. The application resolves the original
text for your FINAL checks. It never converts ledger flags or reference labels into

Use only supplied verified_patient_facts and original guideline_evidence. The nurse
note gives context, not permission to promote unverified or negated findings.
Missing information is not normal. This is not a clinical licensing decision.
Apply the following output-category meanings to the supplied original evidence:
- meets_unconditional_standard: the applicable unconditional requirements are supported;
  do not infer that unknown patient findings are normal.
- may_meet_conditional_standard: the evidence allows a conditional standard and the
  patient facts establish the relevant prerequisites, not just a treatment name.
- temporarily_unfit: an applicable current restriction requires stopping driving
  pending investigation, recovery or stabilisation. Unknown information in another
  module does not erase an already established current restriction.
- does_not_meet_standard: supplied applicable evidence explicitly excludes both
  unconditional AND conditional current eligibility. Failure of an unconditional
  criterion alone does not prove failure of every conditional pathway. This
  category does not itself mean permanent disqualification.
- insufficient_information: no stronger supported restrictive conclusion can be
  established and required facts or applicable guideline evidence are missing.

According to the guideline evidence (PASS-4a8f5a5a5c747d8bd97f4c05, PASS-257a87d15dd2c1b7005a21ef, PASS-c2389eae9eca5bb96ceb386b), a person should not drive for 10 years following two or more blackouts of undetermined nature separated by a 24-hour period. The patient facts confirm `blackout.episodes_separated_by_24h_count = 2` and `blackout.mechanism_status = 'undetermined_after_investigation'`. While the guideline allows for a conditional licence consideration if specific criteria (e.g., 10 years event-free) are met, the current established restriction prohibits driving pending investigation or recovery. The nurse note explicitly states 'Recurrent uncertain blackouts', which establishes an active condition requiring restriction rather than granting normality. The ledger's interpretation of 'not_applicable' for unconditional standards is corrected here: the patient fails the unconditional standard due to the specific blackout history, and while a conditional pathway exists in theory, the immediate clinical state (recurrent uncertain blackouts) mandates a temporary prohibition until the 10-year criterion is verified or further investigation stabilizes the condition. The presence of specialist information does not erase the current restriction; it only enables the review process for potential future eligibility.

The patient has exactly 2 such episodes (`blackout.episodes_separated_by_24h_count = 2`). This explicitly excludes the unconditional standard.
criterion_checks.guideline_quote:
Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods 
driver licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person should not drive for 5 
years following a single blackout of 
undetermined nature.
A person should not drive for 10 years 
following two or more blackouts of 
undetermined nature separated by a 24-
hour period.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has experienced blackouts 
that cannot be diagnosed as syncope, 
seizure or another condition.
If there has been a single blackout or more 
than one blackout within a 24-hour period, 
a conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to 
at least annual review, taking into account 
information provided by an appropriate 
specialist as to whether the following 
criterion is met:
•	 there have been no further blackouts for 
at least 5 years.
If there have been two or more blackouts 
separated by at least 24 hours, a 
conditional licence may be considered by 
the driver licensing authority subject to at 
least annual review, taking into account 
information provided by an appropriate 
specialist as to whether the following 
criterion is met:
•	 there have been no further blackouts for 
at least 10 years.

criterion_checks.conclusion: The guideline states 'A person is not fit to hold an unconditional licence: if the person has experienced blackouts that cannot be diagnosed as syncope, seizure or another condition.' The patient's `blackout.mechanism_status` is 'undetermined_after_investigation' and diagnosis is 'undetermined', confirming they cannot be diagnosed as a specific condition. This excludes the unconditional pathway.

You propose an experimental commercial-driver fitness assessment in English.
Use only supplied verified_patient_facts and original guideline_evidence. The nurse
note gives context, not permission to promote unverified or negated findings.
Missing information is not normal. This is not a clinical licensing decision.
Apply the following output-category meanings to the supplied original evidence:
- meets_unconditional_standard: the applicable unconditional requirements are supported;
  do not infer that unknown patient findings are normal.
- may_meet_conditional_standard: the evidence allows a conditional standard and the
  patient facts establish the relevant prerequisites, not just a treatment name.
- temporarily_unfit: an applicable current restriction requires stopping driving
  pending investigation, recovery or stabilisation. Unknown information in another
  module does not erase an already established current restriction.
- does_not_meet_standard: supplied applicable evidence explicitly excludes both
  unconditional AND conditional current eligibility. Failure of an unconditional
  criterion alone does not prove failure of every conditional pathway. This
  category does not itself mean permanent disqualification.
- insufficient_information: no stronger supported restrictive conclusion can be
  established and required facts or applicable guideline evidence are missing.



This is the aggregation stage. An independent preceding call recorded a proposed
applicability ledger for every supplied original passage. Read the SAME original
facts and passages again. The ledger is fallible: never treat its findings as new
patient facts or as a verified clinical authority. Return your own final criterion
checks, outcome and concise explanation. If a ledger interpretation is wrong,
correct your final check against the ORIGINAL passage and explain the disagreement.
The stored preceding ledger remains unchanged for independent review.

Use the exact scope of each applicable original clause. Distinguish failure of an
unconditional criterion, exclusion of both pathways, and an explicit current
no-driving instruction. A mere referral or missing conditional prerequisite does
not create a temporary prohibition. Unknown findings do not establish normality,
and an unresolved unrelated module does not erase an established restriction.
Do not grant a conditional standard from a possibility or a treatment label when
required qualifications remain unknown. Do not apply an investigation-only rule to
an already diagnosed cause. Do not apply a negated condition to this patient.

Return assessment_outcome, explanation and 1 to 5 criterion_checks using supplied
passage_id, module, fact_fields, licence_pathway, finding and conclusion. Cite only
supplied original passages and verified fields. The application resolves the original
text for your FINAL checks. It never converts ledger flags or reference labels into
the outcome. These checks are your own proposal, not a copy asserted to be verified.

You propose an experimental commercial-driver fitness assessment in English.
Use only supplied verified_patient_facts and original guideline_evidence. The nurse
note gives context, not permission to promote unverified or negated findings.
Missing information is not normal. This is not a clinical licensing decision.
Apply the following output-category meanings to the supplied original evidence:
- meets_unconditional_standard: the applicable unconditional requirements are supported;
  do not infer that unknown patient findings are normal.
- may_meet_conditional_standard: the evidence allows a conditional standard and the
  patient facts establish the relevant prerequisites, not just a treatment name.
- temporarily_unfit: an applicable current restriction requires stopping driving
  pending investigation, recovery or stabilisation. Unknown information in another
  module does not erase an already established current restriction.
- does_not_meet_standard: supplied applicable evidence explicitly excludes both
  unconditional AND conditional current eligibility. Failure of an unconditional
  criterion alone does not prove failure of every conditional pathway. This
  category does not itself mean permanent disqualification.
- insufficient_information: no stronger supported restrictive conclusion can be
  established and required facts or applicable guideline evidence are missing.



This is the aggregation stage. An independent preceding call recorded a proposed
applicability ledger for every supplied original passage. Read the SAME original
facts and passages again. The ledger is fallible: never treat its findings as new
patient facts or as a verified clinical authority. Return your own final criterion
checks, outcome and concise explanation. If a ledger interpretation is wrong,
correct your final check against the ORIGINAL passage and explain the disagreement.
The stored preceding ledger remains unchanged for independent review.

Use the exact scope of each applicable original clause. Distinguish failure of an
unconditional criterion, exclusion of both pathways, and an explicit current
no-driving instruction. A mere referral or missing conditional prerequisite does
not create a temporary prohibition. Unknown findings do not establish normality,
and an unresolved unrelated module does not erase an established restriction.
Do not grant a conditional standard from a possibility or a treatment label when
required qualifications remain unknown. Do not apply an investigation-only rule to
an already diagnosed cause. Do not apply a negated condition to this patient.

Return assessment_outcome, explanation and 1 to 5 criterion_checks using supplied
passage_id, module, fact_fields, licence_pathway, finding and conclusion. Cite only
supplied original passages and verified fields. The application resolves the original
text for your FINAL checks. It never converts ledger flags or reference labels into
the outcome. These checks are your own proposal, not a copy asserted to be verified.

messages.content:
You propose an experimental commercial-driver fitness assessment in English.
Use only supplied verified_patient_facts and original guideline_evidence. The nurse
note gives context, not permission to promote unverified or negated findings.
Missing information is not normal. This is not a clinical licensing decision.
Apply the following output-category meanings to the supplied original evidence:
- meets_unconditional_standard: the applicable unconditional requirements are supported;
  do not infer that unknown patient findings are normal.
- may_meet_conditional_standard: the evidence allows a conditional standard and the
  patient facts establish the relevant prerequisites, not just a treatment name.
- temporarily_unfit: an applicable current restriction requires stopping driving
  pending investigation, recovery or stabilisation. Unknown information in another
  module does not erase an already established current restriction.
- does_not_meet_standard: supplied applicable evidence explicitly excludes both
  unconditional AND conditional current eligibility. Failure of an unconditional
  criterion alone does not prove failure of every conditional pathway. This
  category does not itself mean permanent disqualification.
- insufficient_information: no stronger supported restrictive conclusion can be
  established and required facts or applicable guideline evidence are missing.



This is the aggregation stage. An independent preceding call recorded a proposed
applicability ledger for every supplied original passage. Read the SAME original
facts and passages again. The ledger is fallible: never treat its findings as new
patient facts or as a verified clinical authority. Return your own final criterion
checks, outcome and concise explanation. If a ledger interpretation is wrong,
correct your final check against the ORIGINAL passage and explain the disagreement.
The stored preceding ledger remains unchanged for independent review.

Use the exact scope of each applicable original clause. Distinguish failure of an
unconditional criterion, exclusion of both pathways, and an explicit current
no-driving instruction. A mere referral or missing conditional prerequisite does
not create a temporary prohibition. Unknown findings do not establish normality,
and an unresolved unrelated module does not erase an established restriction.
Do not grant a conditional standard from a possibility or a treatment label when
required qualifications remain unknown. Do not apply an investigation-only rule to
an already diagnosed cause. Do not apply a negated condition to this patient.

Return assessment_outcome, explanation and 1 to 5 criterion_checks using supplied
passage_id, module, fact_fields, licence_pathway, finding and conclusion. Cite only
supplied original passages and verified fields. The application resolves the original
text for your FINAL checks. It never converts ledger flags or reference labels into
the outcome. These checks are your own proposal, not a copy asserted to be verified.

answer.explanation: The patient meets all unconditional criteria for a commercial driver licence. The verified facts confirm the presence of diabetes treated exclusively by diet and exercise, with no history of severe hypoglycaemia, preserved hypoglycaemia awareness, and no driving-relevant end-organ effects. Blood pressure and vision are within normal limits. While the guideline text explicitly states that such patients may drive 'without licence restriction' (unconditional), the assessment also confirms eligibility for a conditional pathway as a safety net; however, since all unconditional prerequisites are met, the outcome is unconditional fitness.

criterion_checks.conclusion: The patient is treated by diet and exercise alone, satisfying the primary prerequisite for an unconditional licence under section 3.3.
criterion_checks.guideline_quote:
Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods driver 
licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person with diabetes treated by diet and 
exercise alone may drive without licence 
restriction. They should he reviewed by their 
treating doctor periodically regarding the 
progression of their diabetes.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has non–insulin treated 
diabetes mellitus and is being treated with 
glucose-lowering agents other than insulin.
A conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to at 
least annual review, taking into consideration 
the nature of the driving task and information 
provided by an endocrinologist or consultant 
physician specialising in diabetes* on whether 
the following criteria are met:
•	 there is no recent history of a ‘severe 
hypoglycaemic event’ as assessed by the 
specialist; and
•	 the person experiences early warning 
symptoms (awareness) of hypoglycaemia; 
and
•	 the person is following a treatment regimen 
that minimises the risk of hypoglycaemia; 
and
•	 there is an absence of end-organ 
effects that may affect driving as per this 
publication.
* For a commercial driver with type 2 diabetes 
who is being treated with metformin alone, the 
annual review for a conditional licence may 
be undertaken by the driver’s treating doctor 
upon mutual agreement of the treating doctor, 
specialist and driver licensing authority. The 
initial granting of a conditional licence must, 
however, be based on information provided by 
the specialist.

criterion_checks.conclusion: The absence of driving-relevant comorbidities (assessed as no disqualifying effect) supports the unconditional standard.

messages.content:
You propose an experimental commercial-driver fitness assessment in English.
Use only supplied verified_patient_facts and original guideline_evidence. The nurse
note gives context, not permission to promote unverified or negated findings.
Missing information is not normal. This is not a clinical licensing decision.
Apply the following output-category meanings to the supplied original evidence:
- meets_unconditional_standard: the applicable unconditional requirements are supported;
  do not infer that unknown patient findings are normal.
- may_meet_conditional_standard: the evidence allows a conditional standard and the
  patient facts establish the relevant prerequisites, not just a treatment name.
- temporarily_unfit: an applicable current restriction requires stopping driving
  pending investigation, recovery or stabilisation. Unknown information in another
  module does not erase an already established current restriction.
- does_not_meet_standard: supplied applicable evidence explicitly excludes both
  unconditional AND conditional current eligibility. Failure of an unconditional
  criterion alone does not prove failure of every conditional pathway. This
  category does not itself mean permanent disqualification.
- insufficient_information: no stronger supported restrictive conclusion can be
  established and required facts or applicable guideline evidence are missing.



This is the aggregation stage. An independent preceding call recorded a proposed
applicability ledger for every supplied original passage. Read the SAME original
facts and passages again. The ledger is fallible: never treat its findings as new
patient facts or as a verified clinical authority. Return your own final criterion
checks, outcome and concise explanation. If a ledger interpretation is wrong,
correct your final check against the ORIGINAL passage and explain the disagreement.
The stored preceding ledger remains unchanged for independent review.

Use the exact scope of each applicable original clause. Distinguish failure of an
unconditional criterion, exclusion of both pathways, and an explicit current
no-driving instruction. A mere referral or missing conditional prerequisite does
not create a temporary prohibition. Unknown findings do not establish normality,
and an unresolved unrelated module does not erase an established restriction.
Do not grant a conditional standard from a possibility or a treatment label when
required qualifications remain unknown. Do not apply an investigation-only rule to
an already diagnosed cause. Do not apply a negated condition to this patient.

Return assessment_outcome, explanation and 1 to 5 criterion_checks using supplied
passage_id, module, fact_fields, licence_pathway, finding and conclusion. Cite only
supplied original passages and verified fields. The application resolves the original
text for your FINAL checks. It never converts ledger flags or reference labels into
the outcome. These checks are your own proposal, not a copy asserted to be verified.

answer.explanation: The patient meets all unconditional criteria for a commercial driver licence. The verified facts confirm the presence of diabetes treated exclusively by diet and exercise, with no history of severe hypoglycaemia, preserved hypoglycaemia awareness, and no driving-relevant end-organ effects. Blood pressure and vision are within normal limits. While the guideline text explicitly states that such patients may drive 'without licence restriction' (unconditional), the assessment also confirms eligibility for a conditional pathway as a safety net; however, since all unconditional prerequisites are met, the outcome is unconditional fitness.

criterion_checks.conclusion: The patient is treated by diet and exercise alone, satisfying the primary prerequisite for an unconditional licence under section 3.3.
criterion_checks.guideline_quote:
Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods driver 
licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person with diabetes treated by diet and 
exercise alone may drive without licence 
restriction. They should he reviewed by their 
treating doctor periodically regarding the 
progression of their diabetes.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has non–insulin treated 
diabetes mellitus and is being treated with 
glucose-lowering agents other than insulin.
A conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to at 
least annual review, taking into consideration 
the nature of the driving task and information 
provided by an endocrinologist or consultant 
physician specialising in diabetes* on whether 
the following criteria are met:
•	 there is no recent history of a ‘severe 
hypoglycaemic event’ as assessed by the 
specialist; and
•	 the person experiences early warning 
symptoms (awareness) of hypoglycaemia; 
and
•	 the person is following a treatment regimen 
that minimises the risk of hypoglycaemia; 
and
•	 there is an absence of end-organ 
effects that may affect driving as per this 
publication.
* For a commercial driver with type 2 diabetes 
who is being treated with metformin alone, the 
annual review for a conditional licence may 
be undertaken by the driver’s treating doctor 
upon mutual agreement of the treating doctor, 
specialist and driver licensing authority. The 
initial granting of a conditional licence must, 
however, be based on information provided by 
the specialist.

criterion_checks.conclusion: The absence of driving-relevant comorbidities (assessed as no disqualifying effect) supports the unconditional standard.

You propose an experimental commercial-driver fitness assessment in English.
Use only supplied verified_patient_facts and original guideline_evidence. The nurse
note gives context, not permission to promote unverified or negated findings.
Missing information is not normal. This is not a clinical licensing decision.
Apply the following output-category meanings to the supplied original evidence:
- meets_unconditional_standard: the applicable unconditional requirements are supported;
  do not infer that unknown patient findings are normal.
- may_meet_conditional_standard: the evidence allows a conditional standard and the
  patient facts establish the relevant prerequisites, not just a treatment name.
- temporarily_unfit: an applicable current restriction requires stopping driving
  pending investigation, recovery or stabilisation. Unknown information in another
  module does not erase an already established current restriction.
- does_not_meet_standard: supplied applicable evidence explicitly excludes both
  unconditional AND conditional current eligibility. Failure of an unconditional
  criterion alone does not prove failure of every conditional pathway. This
  category does not itself mean permanent disqualification.
- insufficient_information: no stronger supported restrictive conclusion can be
  established and required facts or applicable guideline evidence are missing.



This is the aggregation stage. An independent preceding call recorded a proposed
applicability ledger for every supplied original passage. Read the SAME original
facts and passages again. The ledger is fallible: never treat its findings as new
patient facts or as a verified clinical authority. Return your own final criterion
checks, outcome and concise explanation. If a ledger interpretation is wrong,
correct your final check against the ORIGINAL passage and explain the disagreement.
The stored preceding ledger remains unchanged for independent review.

Use the exact scope of each applicable original clause. Distinguish failure of an
unconditional criterion, exclusion of both pathways, and an explicit current
no-driving instruction. A mere referral or missing conditional prerequisite does
not create a temporary prohibition. Unknown findings do not establish normality,
and an unresolved unrelated module does not erase an established restriction.
Do not grant a conditional standard from a possibility or a treatment label when
required qualifications remain unknown. Do not apply an investigation-only rule to
an already diagnosed cause. Do not apply a negated condition to this patient.

Return assessment_outcome, explanation and 1 to 5 criterion_checks using supplied
passage_id, module, fact_fields, licence_pathway, finding and conclusion. Cite only
supplied original passages and verified fields. The application resolves the original
text for your FINAL checks. It never converts ledger flags or reference labels into
the outcome. These checks are your own proposal, not a copy asserted to be verified.

You propose an experimental commercial-driver fitness assessment in English.
Use only supplied verified_patient_facts and original guideline_evidence. The nurse
note gives context, not permission to promote unverified or negated findings.
Missing information is not normal. This is not a clinical licensing decision.
Apply the following output-category meanings to the supplied original evidence:
- meets_unconditional_standard: the applicable unconditional requirements are supported;
  do not infer that unknown patient findings are normal.
- may_meet_conditional_standard: the evidence allows a conditional standard and the
  patient facts establish the relevant prerequisites, not just a treatment name.
- temporarily_unfit: an applicable current restriction requires stopping driving
  pending investigation, recovery or stabilisation. Unknown information in another
  module does not erase an already established current restriction.
- does_not_meet_standard: supplied applicable evidence explicitly excludes both
  unconditional AND conditional current eligibility. Failure of an unconditional
  criterion alone does not prove failure of every conditional pathway. This
  category does not itself mean permanent disqualification.
- insufficient_information: no stronger supported restrictive conclusion can be
  established and required facts or applicable guideline evidence are missing.



This is the aggregation stage. An independent preceding call recorded a proposed
applicability ledger for every supplied original passage. Read the SAME original
facts and passages again. The ledger is fallible: never treat its findings as new
patient facts or as a verified clinical authority. Return your own final criterion
checks, outcome and concise explanation. If a ledger interpretation is wrong,
correct your final check against the ORIGINAL passage and explain the disagreement.
The stored preceding ledger remains unchanged for independent review.

Use the exact scope of each applicable original clause. Distinguish failure of an
unconditional criterion, exclusion of both pathways, and an explicit current
no-driving instruction. A mere referral or missing conditional prerequisite does
not create a temporary prohibition. Unknown findings do not establish normality,
and an unresolved unrelated module does not erase an established restriction.
Do not grant a conditional standard from a possibility or a treatment label when
required qualifications remain unknown. Do not apply an investigation-only rule to
an already diagnosed cause. Do not apply a negated condition to this patient.

Return assessment_outcome, explanation and 1 to 5 criterion_checks using supplied
passage_id, module, fact_fields, licence_pathway, finding and conclusion. Cite only
supplied original passages and verified fields. The application resolves the original
text for your FINAL checks. It never converts ledger flags or reference labels into
the outcome. These checks are your own proposal, not a copy asserted to be verified.

You propose an experimental commercial-driver fitness assessment in English.
Use only supplied verified_patient_facts and original guideline_evidence. The nurse
note gives context, not permission to promote unverified or negated findings.
Missing information is not normal. This is not a clinical licensing decision.
Apply the following output-category meanings to the supplied original evidence:
- meets_unconditional_standard: the applicable unconditional requirements are supported;
  do not infer that unknown patient findings are normal.
- may_meet_conditional_standard: the evidence allows a conditional standard and the
  patient facts establish the relevant prerequisites, not just a treatment name.
- temporarily_unfit: an applicable current restriction requires stopping driving
  pending investigation, recovery or stabilisation. Unknown information in another
  module does not erase an already established current restriction.
- does_not_meet_standard: supplied applicable evidence explicitly excludes both
  unconditional AND conditional current eligibility. Failure of an unconditional
  criterion alone does not prove failure of every conditional pathway. This
  category does not itself mean permanent disqualification.
- insufficient_information: no stronger supported restrictive conclusion can be
  established and required facts or applicable guideline evidence are missing.

applicability ledger for every supplied original passage. Read the SAME original
facts and passages again. The ledger is fallible: never treat its findings as new
patient facts or as a verified clinical authority. Return your own final criterion
checks, outcome and concise explanation. If a ledger interpretation is wrong,
correct your final check against the ORIGINAL passage and explain the disagreement.

not create a temporary prohibition. Unknown findings do not establish normality,

You propose an experimental commercial-driver fitness assessment in English.
Use only supplied verified_patient_facts and original guideline_evidence. The nurse
note gives context, not permission to promote unverified or negated findings.
Missing information is not normal. This is not a clinical licensing decision.
Apply the following output-category meanings to the supplied original evidence:
- meets_unconditional_standard: the applicable unconditional requirements are supported;
  do not infer that unknown patient findings are normal.
- may_meet_conditional_standard: the evidence allows a conditional standard and the
  patient facts establish the relevant prerequisites, not just a treatment name.
- temporarily_unfit: an applicable current restriction requires stopping driving
  pending investigation, recovery or stabilisation. Unknown information in another
  module does not erase an already established current restriction.
- does_not_meet_standard: supplied applicable evidence explicitly excludes both
  unconditional AND conditional current eligibility. Failure of an unconditional
  criterion alone does not prove failure of every conditional pathway. This
  category does not itself mean permanent disqualification.
- insufficient_information: no stronger supported restrictive conclusion can be
  established and required facts or applicable guideline evidence are missing.



This is the aggregation stage. An independent preceding call recorded a proposed
applicability ledger for every supplied original passage. Read the SAME original
facts and passages again. The ledger is fallible: never treat its findings as new
patient facts or as a verified clinical authority. Return your own final criterion
checks, outcome and concise explanation. If a ledger interpretation is wrong,
correct your final check against the ORIGINAL passage and explain the disagreement.
The stored preceding ledger remains unchanged for independent review.

Use the exact scope of each applicable original clause. Distinguish failure of an
unconditional criterion, exclusion of both pathways, and an explicit current
no-driving instruction. A mere referral or missing conditional prerequisite does
not create a temporary prohibition. Unknown findings do not establish normality,
and an unresolved unrelated module does not erase an established restriction.
Do not grant a conditional standard from a possibility or a treatment label when
required qualifications remain unknown. Do not apply an investigation-only rule to
an already diagnosed cause. Do not apply a negated condition to this patient.

Return assessment_outcome, explanation and 1 to 5 criterion_checks using supplied
passage_id, module, fact_fields, licence_pathway, finding and conclusion. Cite only
supplied original passages and verified fields. The application resolves the original
text for your FINAL checks. It never converts ledger flags or reference labels into
the outcome. These checks are your own proposal, not a copy asserted to be verified.

answer.explanation: The patient meets the prerequisite for audiometry (indicated by 'possible_hearing_loss' clinical assessment) and has audiometry available. The unaided hearing threshold is exactly 40 dB, which triggers the restriction on unconditional licensing but does not automatically disqualify the driver if a hearing aid can compensate. Since the specific aided threshold is unknown, an unconditional standard cannot be met (as it requires <40 dB unaided), nor can a definitive conditional standard be granted yet without knowing if the hearing aid brings the threshold below 40 dB. Therefore, the evidence supports a pathway to assess eligibility for a conditional licence pending audiometry results.

criterion_checks.conclusion: The clinical assessment indicates 'possible_hearing_loss', satisfying the prerequisite for referral to audiometry as per guideline AFTD2022-EXP-7f3c434bba3c53df section 4.3.
criterion_checks.guideline_quote:
Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger vehicles 
or requiring a dangerous goods driver licence – 
refer to definition in Table 3)
Compliance with the standard should be clinically 
assessed initially. If the initial clinical assessment 
indicates possible hearing loss, the person should 
be referred for audiometry.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional licence:
•	 if the person has unaided hearing loss ≥ 40 dB 
in the better ear (averaged over the frequencies 
0.5, 1, 2 and 3 KHz).
A conditional licence may be considered by the 
driver licensing authority subject to periodic review*, 
taking into account the nature of the driving task 
and information provided by an ENT specialist or 
audiologist**, as to whether:
•	 the standard is able to be met with a hearing 
aid***.
If the standard is not able to be met with a hearing 
aid, further individualised assessment should be 
offered. 
A conditional licence may be considered by the 
driver licensing authority subject to periodic review*, 
taking into account:
•	 the nature of the driving task; and
•	 information provided by an ENT specialist or 
audiologist**; and
•	 the results of a practical driver assessment if 
required. 
* Stable conditions may not require periodic review. 
** Refer to section 4.2. General assessment and 
management guidelines.
*** In some cases, noise amplification as a result of 
wearing hearing aids may lead to driver distraction 
and may warrant individualised assessment to 
determine fitness to drive without the hearing aid 
(refer to 4.2. General assessment and management 
guidelines).

criterion_checks.conclusion: The unaided average is exactly 40 dB. Per guideline AFTD2022-HEAR-COM-002 section 4.3, a person is not fit for an unconditional licence if unaided hearing loss is ≥40 dB in the better ear. Thus, the unconditional standard is explicitly excluded.

You propose an experimental commercial-driver fitness assessment in English.
Use only supplied verified_patient_facts and original guideline_evidence. The nurse
note gives context, not permission to promote unverified or negated findings.
Missing information is not normal. This is not a clinical licensing decision.
Apply the following output-category meanings to the supplied original evidence:
- meets_unconditional_standard: the applicable unconditional requirements are supported;
  do not infer that unknown patient findings are normal.
- may_meet_conditional_standard: the evidence allows a conditional standard and the
  patient facts establish the relevant prerequisites, not just a treatment name.
- temporarily_unfit: an applicable current restriction requires stopping driving
  pending investigation, recovery or stabilisation. Unknown information in another
  module does not erase an already established current restriction.
- does_not_meet_standard: supplied applicable evidence explicitly excludes both
  unconditional AND conditional current eligibility. Failure of an unconditional
  criterion alone does not prove failure of every conditional pathway. This
  category does not itself mean permanent disqualification.
- insufficient_information: no stronger supported restrictive conclusion can be
  established and required facts or applicable guideline evidence are missing.



This is the aggregation stage. An independent preceding call recorded a proposed
applicability ledger for every supplied original passage. Read the SAME original
facts and passages again. The ledger is fallible: never treat its findings as new
patient facts or as a verified clinical authority. Return your own final criterion
checks, outcome and concise explanation. If a ledger interpretation is wrong,
correct your final check against the ORIGINAL passage and explain the disagreement.
The stored preceding ledger remains unchanged for independent review.

Use the exact scope of each applicable original clause. Distinguish failure of an
unconditional criterion, exclusion of both pathways, and an explicit current
no-driving instruction. A mere referral or missing conditional prerequisite does
not create a temporary prohibition. Unknown findings do not establish normality,
and an unresolved unrelated module does not erase an established restriction.
Do not grant a conditional standard from a possibility or a treatment label when
required qualifications remain unknown. Do not apply an investigation-only rule to
an already diagnosed cause. Do not apply a negated condition to this patient.

supplied original passages and verified fields. The application resolves the original
text for your FINAL checks. It never converts ledger flags or reference labels into
the outcome. These checks are your own proposal, not a copy asserted to be verified.

You propose an experimental commercial-driver fitness assessment in English.
Use only supplied verified_patient_facts and original guideline_evidence. The nurse
note gives context, not permission to promote unverified or negated findings.
Missing information is not normal. This is not a clinical licensing decision.
Apply the following output-category meanings to the supplied original evidence:
- meets_unconditional_standard: the applicable unconditional requirements are supported;
  do not infer that unknown patient findings are normal.
- may_meet_conditional_standard: the evidence allows a conditional standard and the
  patient facts establish the relevant prerequisites, not just a treatment name.
- temporarily_unfit: an applicable current restriction requires stopping driving
  pending investigation, recovery or stabilisation. Unknown information in another
  module does not erase an already established current restriction.
- does_not_meet_standard: supplied applicable evidence explicitly excludes both
  unconditional AND conditional current eligibility. Failure of an unconditional
  criterion alone does not prove failure of every conditional pathway. This
  category does not itself mean permanent disqualification.
- insufficient_information: no stronger supported restrictive conclusion can be
  established and required facts or applicable guideline evidence are missing.



This is the aggregation stage. An independent preceding call recorded a proposed
applicability ledger for every supplied original passage. Read the SAME original
facts and passages again. The ledger is fallible: never treat its findings as new
patient facts or as a verified clinical authority. Return your own final criterion
checks, outcome and concise explanation. If a ledger interpretation is wrong,
correct your final check against the ORIGINAL passage and explain the disagreement.
The stored preceding ledger remains unchanged for independent review.

Use the exact scope of each applicable original clause. Distinguish failure of an
unconditional criterion, exclusion of both pathways, and an explicit current
no-driving instruction. A mere referral or missing conditional prerequisite does
not create a temporary prohibition. Unknown findings do not establish normality,
and an unresolved unrelated module does not erase an established restriction.
Do not grant a conditional standard from a possibility or a treatment label when
required qualifications remain unknown. Do not apply an investigation-only rule to
an already diagnosed cause. Do not apply a negated condition to this patient.

Return assessment_outcome, explanation and 1 to 5 criterion_checks using supplied
passage_id, module, fact_fields, licence_pathway, finding and conclusion. Cite only
supplied original passages and verified fields. The application resolves the original
text for your FINAL checks. It never converts ledger flags or reference labels into
the outcome. These checks are your own proposal, not a copy asserted to be verified.

answer.explanation: The patient meets the prerequisite for audiometry (clinical assessment indicates possible hearing loss) and has access to it. The unaided hearing threshold is exactly at the disqualification limit (40 dB). Per guidelines, this does not automatically disqualify the driver from a *conditional* licence if the standard can be met with a hearing aid. criterion_checks.conclusion: The guideline states that if clinical assessment indicates possible hearing loss, the person should be referred for audiometry. The patient has 'possible_hearing_loss' and audiometry is available.
criterion_checks.guideline_quote:
Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger vehicles 
or requiring a dangerous goods driver licence – 
refer to definition in Table 3)
Compliance with the standard should be clinically 
assessed initially. If the initial clinical assessment 
indicates possible hearing loss, the person should 
be referred for audiometry.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional licence:
•	 if the person has unaided hearing loss ≥ 40 dB 
in the better ear (averaged over the frequencies 
0.5, 1, 2 and 3 KHz).
A conditional licence may be considered by the 
driver licensing authority subject to periodic review*, 
taking into account the nature of the driving task 
and information provided by an ENT specialist or 
audiologist**, as to whether:
•	 the standard is able to be met with a hearing 
aid***.
If the standard is not able to be met with a hearing 
aid, further individualised assessment should be 
offered. 
A conditional licence may be considered by the 
driver licensing authority subject to periodic review*, 
taking into account:
•	 the nature of the driving task; and
•	 information provided by an ENT specialist or 
audiologist**; and
•	 the results of a practical driver assessment if 
required. 
* Stable conditions may not require periodic review. 
** Refer to section 4.2. General assessment and 
management guidelines.
*** In some cases, noise amplification as a result of 
wearing hearing aids may lead to driver distraction 
and may warrant individualised assessment to 
determine fitness to drive without the hearing aid 
(refer to 4.2. General assessment and management 
guidelines).

criterion_checks.conclusion: The guideline states a person is not fit for an unconditional licence if unaided hearing loss ≥ 40 dB. The patient's value is exactly 40.0 dB, which meets the threshold for disqualification from an *unconditional* licence, but does not preclude a *conditional* one if aided.

You propose an experimental commercial-driver fitness assessment in English.
Use only supplied verified_patient_facts and original guideline_evidence. The nurse
note gives context, not permission to promote unverified or negated findings.
Missing information is not normal. This is not a clinical licensing decision.
Apply the following output-category meanings to the supplied original evidence:
- meets_unconditional_standard: the applicable unconditional requirements are supported;
  do not infer that unknown patient findings are normal.
- may_meet_conditional_standard: the evidence allows a conditional standard and the
  patient facts establish the relevant prerequisites, not just a treatment name.
- temporarily_unfit: an applicable current restriction requires stopping driving
  pending investigation, recovery or stabilisation. Unknown information in another
  module does not erase an already established current restriction.
- does_not_meet_standard: supplied applicable evidence explicitly excludes both
  unconditional AND conditional current eligibility. Failure of an unconditional
  criterion alone does not prove failure of every conditional pathway. This
  category does not itself mean permanent disqualification.
- insufficient_information: no stronger supported restrictive conclusion can be
  established and required facts or applicable guideline evidence are missing.



This is the aggregation stage. An independent preceding call recorded a proposed
applicability ledger for every supplied original passage. Read the SAME original
facts and passages again. The ledger is fallible: never treat its findings as new
patient facts or as a verified clinical authority. Return your own final criterion
checks, outcome and concise explanation. If a ledger interpretation is wrong,
correct your final check against the ORIGINAL passage and explain the disagreement.
The stored preceding ledger remains unchanged for independent review.

Use the exact scope of each applicable original clause. Distinguish failure of an
unconditional criterion, exclusion of both pathways, and an explicit current
no-driving instruction. A mere referral or missing conditional prerequisite does
not create a temporary prohibition. Unknown findings do not establish normality,
and an unresolved unrelated module does not erase an established restriction.
Do not grant a conditional standard from a possibility or a treatment label when
required qualifications remain unknown. Do not apply an investigation-only rule to
an already diagnosed cause. Do not apply a negated condition to this patient.

Return assessment_outcome, explanation and 1 to 5 criterion_checks using supplied
passage_id, module, fact_fields, licence_pathway, finding and conclusion. Cite only
supplied original passages and verified fields. The application resolves the original
text for your FINAL checks. It never converts ledger flags or reference labels into
the outcome. These checks are your own proposal, not a copy asserted to be verified.

answer.explanation: The patient meets the prerequisite for audiometry (indicated by 'possible_hearing_loss' clinical assessment) and has audiometry available. The unaided hearing threshold is exactly 40 dB, which triggers the restriction on unconditional licensing but does not automatically disqualify the driver if a hearing aid can compensate. Since the specific aided threshold is unknown, an unconditional standard cannot be met (as it requires <40 dB unaided), nor can a definitive conditional standard be granted yet without knowing if the hearing aid brings the threshold below 40 dB. Therefore, the evidence supports a pathway to assess eligibility for a conditional licence pending audiometry results.

criterion_checks.conclusion: The clinical assessment indicates 'possible_hearing_loss', satisfying the prerequisite for referral to audiometry as per guideline AFTD2022-EXP-7f3c434bba3c53df section 4.3.
criterion_checks.guideline_quote:
Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger vehicles 
or requiring a dangerous goods driver licence – 
refer to definition in Table 3)
Compliance with the standard should be clinically 
assessed initially. If the initial clinical assessment 
indicates possible hearing loss, the person should 
be referred for audiometry.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional licence:
•	 if the person has unaided hearing loss ≥ 40 dB 
in the better ear (averaged over the frequencies 
0.5, 1, 2 and 3 KHz).
A conditional licence may be considered by the 
driver licensing authority subject to periodic review*, 
taking into account the nature of the driving task 
and information provided by an ENT specialist or 
audiologist**, as to whether:
•	 the standard is able to be met with a hearing 
aid***.
If the standard is not able to be met with a hearing 
aid, further individualised assessment should be 
offered. 
A conditional licence may be considered by the 
driver licensing authority subject to periodic review*, 
taking into account:
•	 the nature of the driving task; and
•	 information provided by an ENT specialist or 
audiologist**; and
•	 the results of a practical driver assessment if 
required. 
* Stable conditions may not require periodic review. 
** Refer to section 4.2. General assessment and 
management guidelines.
*** In some cases, noise amplification as a result of 
wearing hearing aids may lead to driver distraction 
and may warrant individualised assessment to 
determine fitness to drive without the hearing aid 
(refer to 4.2. General assessment and management 
guidelines).

criterion_checks.conclusion: The unaided average is exactly 40 dB. Per guideline AFTD2022-HEAR-COM-002 section 4.3, a person is not fit for an unconditional licence if unaided hearing loss is ≥40 dB in the better ear. Thus, the unconditional standard is explicitly excluded.

messages.content:
You propose an experimental commercial-driver fitness assessment in English.
Use only supplied verified_patient_facts and original guideline_evidence. The nurse
note gives context, not permission to promote unverified or negated findings.
Missing information is not normal. This is not a clinical licensing decision.
Apply the following output-category meanings to the supplied original evidence:
- meets_unconditional_standard: the applicable unconditional requirements are supported;
  do not infer that unknown patient findings are normal.
- may_meet_conditional_standard: the evidence allows a conditional standard and the
  patient facts establish the relevant prerequisites, not just a treatment name.
- temporarily_unfit: an applicable current restriction requires stopping driving
  pending investigation, recovery or stabilisation. Unknown information in another
  module does not erase an already established current restriction.
- does_not_meet_standard: supplied applicable evidence explicitly excludes both
  unconditional AND conditional current eligibility. Failure of an unconditional
  criterion alone does not prove failure of every conditional pathway. This
  category does not itself mean permanent disqualification.
- insufficient_information: no stronger supported restrictive conclusion can be
  established and required facts or applicable guideline evidence are missing.



This is the aggregation stage. An independent preceding call recorded a proposed
applicability ledger for every supplied original passage. Read the SAME original
facts and passages again. The ledger is fallible: never treat its findings as new
patient facts or as a verified clinical authority. Return your own final criterion
checks, outcome and concise explanation. If a ledger interpretation is wrong,
correct your final check against the ORIGINAL passage and explain the disagreement.
The stored preceding ledger remains unchanged for independent review.

Use the exact scope of each applicable original clause. Distinguish failure of an
unconditional criterion, exclusion of both pathways, and an explicit current
no-driving instruction. A mere referral or missing conditional prerequisite does
not create a temporary prohibition. Unknown findings do not establish normality,

You propose an experimental commercial-driver fitness assessment in English.
Use only supplied verified_patient_facts and original guideline_evidence. The nurse
note gives context, not permission to promote unverified or negated findings.
Missing information is not normal. This is not a clinical licensing decision.
Apply the following output-category meanings to the supplied original evidence:
- meets_unconditional_standard: the applicable unconditional requirements are supported;
  do not infer that unknown patient findings are normal.
- may_meet_conditional_standard: the evidence allows a conditional standard and the
  patient facts establish the relevant prerequisites, not just a treatment name.
- temporarily_unfit: an applicable current restriction requires stopping driving
  pending investigation, recovery or stabilisation. Unknown information in another
  module does not erase an already established current restriction.
- does_not_meet_standard: supplied applicable evidence explicitly excludes both
  unconditional AND conditional current eligibility. Failure of an unconditional
  criterion alone does not prove failure of every conditional pathway. This
  category does not itself mean permanent disqualification.
- insufficient_information: no stronger supported restrictive conclusion can be
  established and required facts or applicable guideline evidence are missing.



This is the aggregation stage. An independent preceding call recorded a proposed
applicability ledger for every supplied original passage. Read the SAME original
facts and passages again. The ledger is fallible: never treat its findings as new
patient facts or as a verified clinical authority. Return your own final criterion
checks, outcome and concise explanation. If a ledger interpretation is wrong,
correct your final check against the ORIGINAL passage and explain the disagreement.
The stored preceding ledger remains unchanged for independent review.

Use the exact scope of each applicable original clause. Distinguish failure of an
unconditional criterion, exclusion of both pathways, and an explicit current
no-driving instruction. A mere referral or missing conditional prerequisite does
not create a temporary prohibition. Unknown findings do not establish normality,
and an unresolved unrelated module does not erase an established restriction.
Do not grant a conditional standard from a possibility or a treatment label when
required qualifications remain unknown. Do not apply an investigation-only rule to
an already diagnosed cause. Do not apply a negated condition to this patient.

Return assessment_outcome, explanation and 1 to 5 criterion_checks using supplied
passage_id, module, fact_fields, licence_pathway, finding and conclusion. Cite only
supplied original passages and verified fields. The application resolves the original
text for your FINAL checks. It never converts ledger flags or reference labels into
the outcome. These checks are your own proposal, not a copy asserted to be verified.

criterion_checks.guideline_quote:
Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger vehicles 
or requiring a dangerous goods driver licence – 
refer to definition in Table 3)
Compliance with the standard should be clinically 
assessed initially. If the initial clinical assessment 
indicates possible hearing loss, the person should 
be referred for audiometry.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional licence:
•	 if the person has unaided hearing loss ≥ 40 dB 
in the better ear (averaged over the frequencies 
0.5, 1, 2 and 3 KHz).
A conditional licence may be considered by the 
driver licensing authority subject to periodic review*, 
taking into account the nature of the driving task 
and information provided by an ENT specialist or 
audiologist**, as to whether:
•	 the standard is able to be met with a hearing 
aid***.
If the standard is not able to be met with a hearing 
aid, further individualised assessment should be 
offered. 
A conditional licence may be considered by the 
driver licensing authority subject to periodic review*, 
taking into account:
•	 the nature of the driving task; and
•	 information provided by an ENT specialist or 
audiologist**; and
•	 the results of a practical driver assessment if 
required. 
* Stable conditions may not require periodic review. 
** Refer to section 4.2. General assessment and 
management guidelines.
*** In some cases, noise amplification as a result of 
wearing hearing aids may lead to driver distraction 
and may warrant individualised assessment to 
determine fitness to drive without the hearing aid 
(refer to 4.2. General assessment and management 
guidelines).

natural history of the condition. Stable conditions

hearing aid.

You propose an experimental commercial-driver fitness assessment in English.
Use only supplied verified_patient_facts and original guideline_evidence. The nurse
note gives context, not permission to promote unverified or negated findings.
Missing information is not normal. This is not a clinical licensing decision.
Apply the following output-category meanings to the supplied original evidence:
- meets_unconditional_standard: the applicable unconditional requirements are supported;
  do not infer that unknown patient findings are normal.
- may_meet_conditional_standard: the evidence allows a conditional standard and the
  patient facts establish the relevant prerequisites, not just a treatment name.
- temporarily_unfit: an applicable current restriction requires stopping driving
  pending investigation, recovery or stabilisation. Unknown information in another
  module does not erase an already established current restriction.
- does_not_meet_standard: supplied applicable evidence explicitly excludes both
  unconditional AND conditional current eligibility. Failure of an unconditional
  criterion alone does not prove failure of every conditional pathway. This
  category does not itself mean permanent disqualification.
- insufficient_information: no stronger supported restrictive conclusion can be
  established and required facts or applicable guideline evidence are missing.

applicability ledger for every supplied original passage. Read the SAME original
facts and passages again. The ledger is fallible: never treat its findings as new
patient facts or as a verified clinical authority. Return your own final criterion
checks, outcome and concise explanation. If a ledger interpretation is wrong,
correct your final check against the ORIGINAL passage and explain the disagreement.
The stored preceding ledger remains unchanged for independent review.

Use the exact scope of each applicable original clause. Distinguish failure of an
unconditional criterion, exclusion of both pathways, and an explicit current
no-driving instruction. A mere referral or missing conditional prerequisite does
not create a temporary prohibition. Unknown findings do not establish normality,
and an unresolved unrelated module does not erase an established restriction.
Do not grant a conditional standard from a possibility or a treatment label when
required qualifications remain unknown. Do not apply an investigation-only rule to
an already diagnosed cause. Do not apply a negated condition to this patient.

supplied original passages and verified fields. The application resolves the original
text for your FINAL checks. It never converts ledger flags or reference labels into
the outcome. These checks are your own proposal, not a copy asserted to be verified.

10.2.2. Visual fields3–6,8–13
For the purposes of this publication, visual 
fields are defined as a measure of the extent 
of peripheral (side) vision. Normal visual field is: 
60 degrees nasally, 100 degrees temporally, 75 
degrees inferiorly and 60 degrees superiorly. 
The binocular field extends the horizontal extent 
from 160 to 200 degrees, with the central 120 
degrees overlapping and providing the potential 
for stereopsis. 
Visual fields may be reduced due to a range 
of neurological conditions (e.g. stroke, multiple 
sclerosis) as well by ocular diseases (e.g. 
glaucoma), or injuries, resulting in hemionopia, 
quadrantanopia or monocularity. 
Peripheral vision assists the driver to be aware 
of the total driving environment. Once alerted, 
the central fovea area is moved to identify 
the importance of the information. Therefore, 
peripheral vision loss that is incomplete will 
still allow awareness; this includes small areas 
of loss and patchy loss. Additionally, affected 
drivers can adapt to the defect by scanning 
regularly and effectively and can have good 
awareness. Patients with visual field defects 
who have full intellectual/cognitive capacity 
are more able to adapt, but those with such 
impairments will have decreased awareness and 
are therefore not safe to drive.
A longstanding field defect, such as from 
childhood, may lead to visual adaptation. Such 
defects need to be assessed by an optometrist 
or ophthalmologist for a conditional licence 
to be considered. They should be managed 
as an exceptional case to the standard, with 
consideration for duration and evidence of visual 
adaptation, whether the location of the defect is 
an area that may already be blocked by the car 
door on the passenger side (i.e. the inferior field 
on the left side without central field loss), driver 
safety record and the nature of the driving task.

messages.content:
You propose an experimental commercial-driver fitness assessment in English.
Use only supplied verified_patient_facts and original guideline_evidence. The nurse
note gives context, not permission to promote unverified or negated findings.
Missing information is not normal. This is not a clinical licensing decision.
Apply the following output-category meanings to the supplied original evidence:
- meets_unconditional_standard: the applicable unconditional requirements are supported;
  do not infer that unknown patient findings are normal.
- may_meet_conditional_standard: the evidence allows a conditional standard and the
  patient facts establish the relevant prerequisites, not just a treatment name.
- temporarily_unfit: an applicable current restriction requires stopping driving
  pending investigation, recovery or stabilisation. Unknown information in another
  module does not erase an already established current restriction.
- does_not_meet_standard: supplied applicable evidence explicitly excludes both
  unconditional AND conditional current eligibility. Failure of an unconditional
  criterion alone does not prove failure of every conditional pathway. This
  category does not itself mean permanent disqualification.
- insufficient_information: no stronger supported restrictive conclusion can be
  established and required facts or applicable guideline evidence are missing.



This is the aggregation stage. An independent preceding call recorded a proposed
applicability ledger for every supplied original passage. Read the SAME original
facts and passages again. The ledger is fallible: never treat its findings as new
patient facts or as a verified clinical authority. Return your own final criterion
checks, outcome and concise explanation. If a ledger interpretation is wrong,
correct your final check against the ORIGINAL passage and explain the disagreement.
The stored preceding ledger remains unchanged for independent review.

Use the exact scope of each applicable original clause. Distinguish failure of an
unconditional criterion, exclusion of both pathways, and an explicit current
no-driving instruction. A mere referral or missing conditional prerequisite does
not create a temporary prohibition. Unknown findings do not establish normality,
and an unresolved unrelated module does not erase an established restriction.
Do not grant a conditional standard from a possibility or a treatment label when
required qualifications remain unknown. Do not apply an investigation-only rule to
an already diagnosed cause. Do not apply a negated condition to this patient.

Return assessment_outcome, explanation and 1 to 5 criterion_checks using supplied
passage_id, module, fact_fields, licence_pathway, finding and conclusion. Cite only
supplied original passages and verified fields. The application resolves the original
text for your FINAL checks. It never converts ledger flags or reference labels into
the outcome. These checks are your own proposal, not a copy asserted to be verified.

criterion_checks.guideline_quote:
10.2.2. Visual fields3–6,8–13
For the purposes of this publication, visual 
fields are defined as a measure of the extent 
of peripheral (side) vision. Normal visual field is: 
60 degrees nasally, 100 degrees temporally, 75 
degrees inferiorly and 60 degrees superiorly. 
The binocular field extends the horizontal extent 
from 160 to 200 degrees, with the central 120 
degrees overlapping and providing the potential 
for stereopsis. 
Visual fields may be reduced due to a range 
of neurological conditions (e.g. stroke, multiple 
sclerosis) as well by ocular diseases (e.g. 
glaucoma), or injuries, resulting in hemionopia, 
quadrantanopia or monocularity. 
Peripheral vision assists the driver to be aware 
of the total driving environment. Once alerted, 
the central fovea area is moved to identify 
the importance of the information. Therefore, 
peripheral vision loss that is incomplete will 
still allow awareness; this includes small areas 
of loss and patchy loss. Additionally, affected 
drivers can adapt to the defect by scanning 
regularly and effectively and can have good 
awareness. Patients with visual field defects 
who have full intellectual/cognitive capacity 
are more able to adapt, but those with such 
impairments will have decreased awareness and 
are therefore not safe to drive.
A longstanding field defect, such as from 
childhood, may lead to visual adaptation. Such 
defects need to be assessed by an optometrist 
or ophthalmologist for a conditional licence 
to be considered. They should be managed 
as an exceptional case to the standard, with 
consideration for duration and evidence of visual 
adaptation, whether the location of the defect is 
an area that may already be blocked by the car 
door on the passenger side (i.e. the inferior field 
on the left side without central field loss), driver 
safety record and the nature of the driving task.

messages.content:
You propose an experimental commercial-driver fitness assessment in English.
Use only supplied verified_patient_facts and original guideline_evidence. The nurse
note gives context, not permission to promote unverified or negated findings.
Missing information is not normal. This is not a clinical licensing decision.
Apply the following output-category meanings to the supplied original evidence:
- meets_unconditional_standard: the applicable unconditional requirements are supported;
  do not infer that unknown patient findings are normal.
- may_meet_conditional_standard: the evidence allows a conditional standard and the
  patient facts establish the relevant prerequisites, not just a treatment name.
- temporarily_unfit: an applicable current restriction requires stopping driving
  pending investigation, recovery or stabilisation. Unknown information in another
  module does not erase an already established current restriction.
- does_not_meet_standard: supplied applicable evidence explicitly excludes both
  unconditional AND conditional current eligibility. Failure of an unconditional
  criterion alone does not prove failure of every conditional pathway. This
  category does not itself mean permanent disqualification.
- insufficient_information: no stronger supported restrictive conclusion can be
  established and required facts or applicable guideline evidence are missing.



This is the aggregation stage. An independent preceding call recorded a proposed
applicability ledger for every supplied original passage. Read the SAME original
facts and passages again. The ledger is fallible: never treat its findings as new
patient facts or as a verified clinical authority. Return your own final criterion
checks, outcome and concise explanation. If a ledger interpretation is wrong,
correct your final check against the ORIGINAL passage and explain the disagreement.
The stored preceding ledger remains unchanged for independent review.

Use the exact scope of each applicable original clause. Distinguish failure of an
unconditional criterion, exclusion of both pathways, and an explicit current
no-driving instruction. A mere referral or missing conditional prerequisite does
not create a temporary prohibition. Unknown findings do not establish normality,
and an unresolved unrelated module does not erase an established restriction.
Do not grant a conditional standard from a possibility or a treatment label when
required qualifications remain unknown. Do not apply an investigation-only rule to
an already diagnosed cause. Do not apply a negated condition to this patient.

Return assessment_outcome, explanation and 1 to 5 criterion_checks using supplied
passage_id, module, fact_fields, licence_pathway, finding and conclusion. Cite only
supplied original passages and verified fields. The application resolves the original
text for your FINAL checks. It never converts ledger flags or reference labels into
the outcome. These checks are your own proposal, not a copy asserted to be verified.

10.2.3. Diplopia
People suffering from all but minor forms of 
diplopia are generally not fit to drive. Any person

criterion_checks.guideline_quote:
Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods 
driver licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person’s uncorrected visual acuity is 
worse than 6/9 in the better eye; or

worse than 6/18 in either eye.
A conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to 
periodic review if the standard is met with 
corrective lenses*.

account:

optometrist or ophthalmologist.
* Refer to section 10.2.7. Orthokeratology 
therapy for information on meeting the 
standard using orthokeratology therapy.
